newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Little growth in retail sales trend in Aug - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Little growth in retail sales trend in Aug - SNZ.

text.p: The underlying trend in New Zealand retail sales grew only 0.1 percent between July and August 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.

Seasonally-adjusted retail sales fell 0.6 percent to NZ$3.22 billion in August. Excluding both automotive storetypes, seasonally-adjusted sales were unchanged at $2.21 billion. Motor vehicle retailing fell a seasonally-adjusted 2.7 percent, while motor vehicle services were down 0.6 percent.

Eight of the 15 storetypes recorded seasonally-adjusted decreases in August, with the largest in the "other stores" group, down 7.1 percent, followed by footwear stores, down 6.3 percent, and appliance retailing outlets, down 5.4 percent.

In the year to August 1996 actual retail sales rose 2.3 percent, or $69.8 million, to reach $3.15 billion. Ten of the 15 storetypes recorded increases over the year, with the fastest rates of growth in hardware stores (up 18 pct); furniture and floorcovering stores (up 13.3 pct); and cafes, restaurants and takeaway outlets (up 11.9 pct).
Food retailing outlets contributed 63 percent, or $44 million, of the total annual increase in actual retail sales.
Actual retail sales excluding both automotive storetypes rose 3.9 percent over the year to August, to NZ$2.11 billion.
Total sales in the South Island rose 2.8 percent in the year, while North Island sales were up 2.1 percent.
